correctness.rationale: Direct coordinate sets give degree six and two common neighbors for every pair of distinct vertices (hence the same strongly regular spectrum). After the first accepted vertex there are nine free vertices, and after any nonadjacent second vertex four. Sorting their induced degrees gives nine cycles on the rook graph and on Shrikhande three cycles (the three specified second choices) and six diamonds. Only the latter can stop at three, and do so half the time. Each permissible ordered triple of early acceptances has probability 1/(16·9·4); a terminal triple has six orders and a terminal quadruple 24, because in the latter case the fourth vertex is the sole free vertex after the third. This gives the claimed labeled probabilities, counts and means. Independently of the packaged subset DP, exponential memorylessness gives independent stages with rates 16, 9 and 4 up to the third acceptance, and with rate 1 when a fourth is possible. Each free vertex is unattempted, and the waiting time for its minimum clock is independent of which free vertex is selected. Thus the mean gap is one third the CDF of the sum of independent exponentials of rates 16,9,4,1. With q=exp(−t), partial fractions give (1−8q/5+4q⁴/5−8q⁹/35+q¹⁶/35)/3. Expanding q^j using (p+q)^(16−j)=1 exactly reconstructed all 17 coefficients and both boundaries, including zero at t=0, the first term 8p⁴ and limiting gap 1/3.
